sections.title: What you will learn to say

blocks.text: So far the sentences were about what people are like and where they are: I am ready, it is here. Now they are about what people do: «I work in a pharmacy», «we mow the lawn», «he drives to work». These are things that happen again and again: jobs, habits, daily life.

examples.translation: My job is in a pharmacy.
We cut the grass.
He goes to work by car.
English is her job.

blocks.text: Here you don't need am, is or are. The action comes right after who: I work, we bake. The most common mistake is to keep the clip out of habit: I am work. That's wrong.

examples.translation: My job is in a pharmacy.
I make bread in the oven.
You clean the floor with a brush.
We cut the hedge to make it neat.
They make a wall.

fixes.wrong: I am work in a pharmacy.

drill.question: You say where you work. Which is correct?
drill.optionA: I am work in a pharmacy.
drill.explain: With an action, you don't need am: I work.

sections.title: I, you, we, they — the action as in the dictionary

blocks.text: With I, you, we and they, the action doesn't change. It's the same as in the dictionary: work, wash, carry.

examples.translation: I clean the plates.
You hold the trays and walk.
We take pears from the tree.
They make holes in the ground.

examples.en: We play football in the yard.
examples.translation: We kick a ball outside.
I go on a bike.

sections.title: He, she, it — add s at the end

blocks.text: With he, she, it, or one person — the host, my brother — the action gets s: he drives, she waits, the host greets. This is the only change, so it's easy to forget. He drive is the most common mistake in this lesson.

examples.translation: He goes to work by car.

examples.en: She waits at the bus stop.
examples.translation: She stays there until the bus comes.
She looks at the baby with a smile.
He tries a little soup.
The host says hello to the guests.
The cat sleeps on the quilt.

fixes.wrong: She wait at the bus stop.
fixes.right: She waits at the bus stop.

drill.why: With she, the action gets s.

blocks.text: If the action ends in sh, ch, s or x, you can't just add s. Add es, and the word gets one more beat: wash → washes, catch → catches, teach → teaches, fish → fishes, mix → mixes.

examples.translation: English is her job.
She gets on the bus in time.
He catches fish with a long stick and line.
She cleans the small plates.

blocks.text: If the action ends in y and there is a consonant before it, change y to ies: study → studies, carry → carries. If there is a vowel before y, just add s: play → plays.

examples.translation: A teacher helps her learn.
He holds a bundle and walks.
He kicks a ball in a game.

drill.why: There's a consonant (d) before y, so y becomes ies.

sections.title: For things that happen again and again

blocks.text: These sentences are about jobs, habits and things that repeat: I walk to work — usually, every day. They are not about what is happening right now, this second.

examples.translation: I go to work on foot.
I go to work by bike.
I do sport at home.
Her home is a flat.
Lamps are what they sell.

sections.title: Where and when — at the end

blocks.text: Where and when usually go at the end: I start at two, She reads in the armchair. Times go with at: at two, at five.

examples.translation: My work begins at two o'clock.
I get there at five o'clock.
She goes away at four o'clock.
She sits in the armchair with a book.
We run early, when the sun comes up.

blocks.text: If there is an action, there is no clip: She cooks. If there is no action and you say who or what someone is, you need the clip and a: She is an artist. Both together are wrong: She is cooks.

examples.translation: Art is her job.
He makes pictures of people.
Making bread is his job.
The tailor fixes uniforms.
I'm new at this.

drill.prompt: Say that the tailor fixes uniforms.

fixes.wrong: I am work in a pharmacy.

blocks.text: Two checks. Is there an action? Then remove am, is, are. Is it he, she, it or one person? Then add s.
Who + action, no clip. I, you, we, they — the action as in the dictionary. He, she, it — add s, sometimes es or ies. Where and when at the end; times with at.

examples.translation: We put things into the bags.
He has a cough.
She gets on the bus in time.
A teacher helps her learn.
I get there at five o'clock.
